Data:Bust.abbot.geffrey.json.Label: 'Abbot Geffrey'
Data:Bust.abbot.geffrey.json.Desc: It was Abbot Geffrey who gave Natan of Regensburg sanctuary here, and decreed the building of the Barber's Tower where Natan and his family could dwell. In fifteenth-century England, only a determined and well-respected abbot could have persuaded the brothers to shelter a Jewish physician.

xexts.scrutiny: The bust is carved from hazel wood. The night before Natan's arrival at the Isle, Abbot Geffrey recorded a certain prophetic dream… and there is an old tradition in this country concerning the prophetic virtues of hazel. Perhaps none of these things are related.

Data:Bust.abbot.thomas.json.Label: 'Abbot Thomas'
Data:Bust.abbot.thomas.json.Desc: Thomas was one of the first abbots here, just before the beginning of the Solar Gothic period. This bust is much more recent - a nineteenth-century bronze. An inscription reads: SPEECH, THE FIRST SWORD.

xexts.scrutiny: The Abbey chronicles record how Viking mercenaries were quartered at the Abbey. One of their number, Toke, attempted to loot the church, and his eyes are pecked out by 'thorn-beaked crows'. He repented, became a sworn brother of the abbey under the name Thomas, and rose in time to be Abbot. But that was not the end of his story...
The sculpture is signed 'SB'.

Data:Bust.abra.json.Label: Pale Bust
Data:Bust.abra.json.Desc: A delicate-featured young (?) woman. An inscription reads ABRA SOUTHEY.

xexts.scrutiny: The bust bears a slight but definite resemblance to the many depictions of the notorious Eva Dewulf. But surely Eva bore only a son, and her grand-daughters died young.

Data:Bust.ambrose.json.Label: 'Ambrose Westcott'
Data:Bust.ambrose.json.Desc: This bust is cast in brass.

xexts.scrutiny: Ambrose Westcott, first Librarian of Hush House: metallurgist, alchemist, pyrographer.

Data:Bust.brian.json.Label: 'Brian Levinsen'
Data:Bust.brian.json.Desc: This bust is cast from aluminium - oxidised to grey.

xexts.scrutiny: Brian Levinsen, ninth Librarian, painter and doctor, who never returned from the Western Front.

Data:Bust.david.json.Label: 'Sir David Greene'
Data:Bust.david.json.Desc: This bust is carved from reddish granite.

xexts.scrutiny: Sir David Greene, eighth Librarian - a former Nocturnal Branch superintendent, better known for rooting out mysteries than illuminating them.

Data:Bust.eva.json.Label: 'Eva Dewulf'
Data:Bust.eva.json.Desc: This is the crystal called scolecite - the worm-stone - polished to chill smoothness.

xexts.scrutiny: Baroness Eva - satirist, salonnière, herpetologist, and last of the Dewulfs.

Data:Bust.fraser.json.Label: 'Fraser Strathcoyne'
Data:Bust.fraser.json.Desc: This bust is shaped from beeswax. Careful with it!

xexts.scrutiny: Fraser Strathcoyne, 'the Collector', formerly Treasurer of the Curia and (briefly, in the absence of other candidates, and to his annoyance) fourth Librarian.

Data:Bust.gervinus.json.Label: 'Gervinus van Lauren'
Data:Bust.gervinus.json.Desc: This bust is cast in highly polished bronze.

xexts.scrutiny: Gervinus van Lauren, eleventh Librarian of Hush House: an enigmatic recluse and reluctant ally of the Suppression Bureau, as skilled at closing ways as his predecessor Harries was at opening them.

Data:Bust.gideon.json.Label: 'Gideon Dewulf'
Data:Bust.gideon.json.Desc: The bust is terracotta, brightly painted.

xexts.scrutiny: Gideon the physician, fifth of his line, nicknamed 'the Motley Baron' by those who disliked him and 'the Cutter' by those who feared him.

Data:Bust.hendrik.json.Label: 'Hendrik Dewulf'
Data:Bust.hendrik.json.Desc: Hendrik Dewulf, 1st Baron Brancrug, known for his pious, merciless justice. Granted Brancrug Isle in 1536 after the dissolution of St Brandan's.

xexts.scrutiny: Dewulf had been a mercenary captain on the Continent, under the notorious Maarten van Rossum. He was a hard man in a hard time, but not a simple one. He left van Rossum's service after the sack of the Hague, apparently after a spiritual crisis;  it is known that he was at one point in training as a priest.

Data:Bust.kitty.json.Label: 'Kitty Mazarine'
Data:Bust.kitty.json.Desc: This bust is carved from black limestone.

xexts.scrutiny: Kitty Mazarine, second Librarian - musician, composer, one-time placée. 'Almost French, almost Spanish, or almost American.'
A forgotten Name of the Velvet?
A forgotten Name of the Moth?
